info.title: VeraHub publisher API
info.description:
The API publishers' backends and apps call. Preview: it may still change, with notice, and a route whose feature is not built yet answers `501`.

Paths under `/v1/me` answer browsers on any origin (CORS, without credentials), so apps in a web view can call them: they accept `Authorization`, `Content-Type`, `VeraHub-Client`, and `VeraHub-Expected-User` and expose `Retry-After` and `X-Request-Id`. Every other path sends no CORS headers, so an API key never works from a browser. A preflight (`OPTIONS`) anywhere under `/v1/me` answers `204` for the methods `GET`, `HEAD`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `POST`, and `DELETE`, cacheable for 7200 seconds (browsers cap it lower). Every response under `/v1/me` belongs to one user and carries `Cache-Control: private, no-store`.

Every response a route answers carries `X-Request-Id`: the `X-Request-Id` the request sent, when it is 1 to 128 letters, digits, `_`, `.`, `:`, or `-`, and a new id otherwise; preflights and requests refused before a route answers (an unreadable body, a malformed URL) carry none. Browsers cannot send it: it is not an allowed CORS header. Quote it when reporting a problem.

parameters.description: Your stable, opaque id for the user: 1 to 128 characters from `A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ ~ -`, the first a letter or digit, case-sensitive. Never an email address or anything else that identifies the person directly.

delete.summary: Delete a user: their tokens stop working at once, and a later token request creates a new user without holdings or consent. Answers 204 whether or not the user existed

get.summary: Get the user's consent; both flags are false until the app sets them

put.summary: Replace the user's consent as a whole

post.summary: Reveal a coupon for the user: returns their code, the same one again when they already hold it. Safe to retry: a repeated request never hands out a second code

parameters.name: benefitKinds
parameters.description: The benefit kinds your app can show, repeated for several (`benefitKinds=coupon`). Required: only these kinds are returned, and lists and counts are computed from them, so a kind added later never reaches an app that was not built for it. A kind the API does not know is refused.

displayHint.description: The key's prefix and last 4 characters, e.g. `verahub_sk_...MYPq`.

lastUsedAt.description: When the key last authenticated a request, to the hour.

revokedAt.description: When the key was revoked; it authenticates nothing since.

kind.description: The benefit kind. Fields specific to one kind, if it has any, sit in a part named after it.

valueText.description: The short value, up to 16 characters, e.g. "25 %".

title.description: Up to 60 characters, e.g. "25 % auf Wanderschuhe".

conditions.description: What applies to it, up to 500 characters. Make it reachable before the user reveals the benefit.

endsAt.description: When it can no longer be revealed; absent while no end is set.

nextRevealAt.description: While a cooldown runs, when the user can reveal this benefit for a new code. Absent when a reveal answers at once: with a new holding, or with the one they hold for good.

clickOut.description: Where a tap leads; always present for a coupon.

logoWide.description: 3:1, 768 × 256, on an opaque background; fall back to `logo`.

key.description: The category's key, e.g. `sports-outdoors`: a stable identifier that never changes and is never reused. Show the categories the API returns, not a fixed set of your own; to attach your own icons, map the keys you know and show a fallback for one you do not. Keys can be added and retired.

name.description: The German name, which can change.

offerCount.description: The number of offers the offer list returns when the same caller filters by this category with the same `benefitKinds`; can be 0. Hide a category with a count of 0.

items.description: Every category, every time, in VeraHub's fixed order (reorder them if you like), each with its count, also when it is 0. Categories can be added and retired: build your categories from this list and do not rely on how many there are.

url.description: Open it unaltered in the system browser or an in-app browser tab (SFSafariViewController, Custom Tabs), never in a web view. Valid as long as the app shows the offer; fetch it again with the offer.

id.description: The app's own id for the event, unique per user: an event sent twice counts once, so a retry is safe.

name.description: `offerViewed`: an offer was at least half visible for one second; properties `offerId` and `feedId` (the list's `feedId`, up to 24 hours after that feed was loaded). Events with a name the API does not know are dropped, not refused.

occurredAt.description: When it happened, by the device's clock.

properties.description: The event's properties, by its name; string values.

analytics.description: Whether the user's activity may be measured.

personalisation.description: Whether offers may be personalised to the user.

updatedAt.description: When the app last set the consent; absent while it never has.

userId.description: Your stable, opaque id for the user: 1 to 128 characters from `A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ ~ -`, the first a letter or digit, case-sensitive. Never an email address or anything else that identifies the person directly.

country.description: The user's country, which decides the offers they are shown.

listed.description: Whether the offer is listed for the user now, so its detail can be opened.

kind.description: The benefit kind, which names the part below that carries the rest.

expiresAt.description: When it stops working at the brand's shop; absent if it never does.

expired.description: Whether `expiresAt` has passed. Expired holdings stay; hide them if you like.

clickOut.description: Where a tap leads; always present for a coupon.

code.description: The code to enter at the brand's checkout. Show it unaltered.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; absent on the last page. Opaque: do not build or store it.

url.description: Absolute and immutable; do not build or alter it. A replaced image gets a new URL.

valueText.description: The short value, up to 16 characters, e.g. "bis zu 25 %".

title.description: Up to 60 characters, e.g. "25 % auf Wanderschuhe".

images.description: One image in three ratios; use the one your layout needs.

categories.description: One to three, the offer's main category first.

benefits.description: Every benefit the user can get from the offer, of the requested kinds, in VeraHub's order.

Offer.description: An offer's texts can differ per user and per request: do not cache them across users. Texts are German plain text.

key.description: The category's key, e.g. `sports-outdoors`: a stable identifier that never changes and is never reused. Show the categories the API returns, not a fixed set of your own; to attach your own icons, map the keys you know and show a fallback for one you do not. Keys can be added and retired.

name.description: The German name, which can change.

offer.description: The offer in the same shape as in the list.

user.description: What belongs to this user, kept apart from the offer.

benefits.description: One entry per benefit in `offer.benefits`: when the user can reveal it, and where a tap leads.

holdings.description: What the user holds from any of the offer's benefits, newest first, also from benefits no longer listed.

feedId.description: This feed load's id, the same on every page of it. Offer views name it (`POST /v1/me/events`); a new load from the first page gets a new one.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; absent on the last page. Opaque: do not build or store it.

type.description: URI reference identifying the problem type: `/problems/<code>`, or `about:blank` for plain HTTP errors.

code.description: The problem's code, the last segment of `type`: branch on it. Codes are part of the compatibility promise; new ones can appear. Absent on plain HTTP errors (`about:blank`).

detail.description: A description for developers, in English. Never show it to users.

requestId.description: The request's id, the same as the `X-Request-Id` header. Quote it when reporting a problem. Absent when the response carries no `X-Request-Id`.

targetIds.description: The ids of what the problem is about, named like the parameters that take them.

errors.description: Each invalid field of a rejected request.

nextRevealAt.description: When the user can reveal again; only on `user-limit-reached`.

analytics.description: Whether the user's activity may be measured.

personalisation.description: Whether offers may be personalised to the user.

outcome.description: `allocated`: the user received the holding now. `already-held`: they hold it already, and it is returned again. `cooldown`: they may get a new code only from `nextRevealAt`; the holding is their latest. Treat an outcome you do not know as a success: it comes with a holding.

nextRevealAt.description: When the user can reveal this benefit for a new code; absent when they never can (it is held for good).

sentAt.description: When this request is sent, by the device's clock, the same clock as `occurredAt`. Set it anew on every retry.

token.description: The user token for your app, `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Opaque: do not read its contents.

VeraHubClient.name: VeraHub-Client
VeraHubClient.description: What the request comes from, as a structured field dictionary (RFC 9651) of ASCII strings (`appearance="dark"`, never a bare token or a display string; the SDKs drop or replace other characters): `sdk` (SDK name and version), `os` (platform and OS version), `app` (app version), `build` (app build), `device` (device model), `locale` (BCP 47), `tz` (IANA time zone), `screen` (screen size class), `text-size` (text size setting), `appearance` (`light` or `dark`), and `network` (connection type). Every name is optional; unknown names, values over 128 characters, and other types are ignored, a header that does not parse (a non-ASCII character, for one) is ignored as a whole, and more names can be added. The SDKs send it on every request; an app that calls the API without an SDK sends it itself. `sdk` is `<sdk name>/<version>`, the name in lowercase (`swift/0.3.0`): an SDK version that is no longer served gets `403` `sdk-unsupported`, only for a security problem or a removed API version and announced at least 6 months ahead. A request without `sdk` is served.
VeraHubClient.example: sdk="swift/0.3.0", os="ios/18.2", app="5.4.1", build="5410", locale="de-DE", tz="Europe/Berlin"

VeraHubExpectedUser.name: VeraHub-Expected-User
VeraHubExpectedUser.description: The `userId` the app believes it acts for. A user token of another user is refused with `403` `user-mismatch`, so a token left over from before a user switch never shows one user another's coupons. Any other value, a malformed one included, gets `user-mismatch`; without the header the request is served. The SDKs always send it.

UserCacheControl.description: The response belongs to one user; no cache keeps it.

userToken.description: A user token from `POST /v1/user-tokens`: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Only paths under `/v1/me` take it. It is checked before anything else the route checks or does, so `401` `user-token-expired` comes first: fetch a new token and retry once. Then come `sdk-unsupported`, `user-mismatch`, and `user-not-found`, in this order. Only a body the server cannot read at all is refused before the token, with no `code`: malformed JSON (`400`), an unsupported charset or content encoding (`415`), or a body too large (`413`).
